scope: Homepage Trending eligibility only; safety, security, privacy, fairness, truthfulness and safety-relevant robustness. Catalog membership is unchanged.

records.name: BIPIA
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates indirect prompt injection through external content and defenses against attacker-controlled instructions.

records.name: ToolEmu
records.reason: The primary paper introduces emulated tools and a safety evaluator to identify agent failures such as private-data leakage and financial loss.

records.name: InjecAgent
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates indirect prompt injections intended to harm users or exfiltrate private data through tool-integrated agents.

records.name: AgentDojo
records.reason: The primary paper measures agent security against prompt injections in untrusted tool outputs and provides attack and defense evaluation tasks.

records.name: AgentHarm
records.reason: The primary paper tests refusal and completion of explicitly malicious multi-step agent tasks across harm categories.

records.name: RedCode
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates risky code execution and generation, including unsafe file-system operations and harmful software.

records.name: VPI-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper tests whether malicious instructions embedded in rendered interfaces hijack computer-use and browser agents.

records.name: R-Judge
records.reason: The primary paper measures recognition and identification of safety risks from annotated agent interaction records.

records.name: SALAD-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper explicitly evaluates LLM safety and attack/defense performance through a hierarchical risk taxonomy.

records.name: h4rm3l
records.reason: The primary paper synthesizes compositional jailbreaks and benchmarks harmful model behavior against the resulting attack dataset.

records.name: SG-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper measures safety alignment generalization across generative and discriminative tasks, prompting styles, and jailbreaks.

records.name: ChemSafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates chemical-response safety, legality, accuracy, and dangerous synthesis requests, including jailbreak scenarios.

records.name: ToolSword
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safety failures across tool-learning input, execution, and output stages, including harmful requests and risky tools.

records.name: PrivacyLens
records.reason: The primary paper measures contextual privacy norms and sensitive-information leakage in agents' actual actions.

records.name: SafeBench
records.reason: The primary paper explicitly evaluates autonomous-driving safety using generated safety-critical scenarios and adversarial/distribution-shift testing.

records.name: Agent Security Bench (ASB)
records.reason: The primary paper benchmarks agent prompt injection, memory poisoning, backdoors, and defenses across operational stages.

records.name: SafeAgentBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safety-aware embodied task planning under explicit and implicit hazards in interactive simulation.

records.name: Agent-SafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates agent safety risks and unsafe interaction failure modes across tool environments.

records.name: AdvWeb / ARE
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates targeted adversarial hijacking of multimodal web agents through manipulated image observations.

records.name: ST-WebAgentBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates policy-compliant web-agent completion and violations involving consent, robustness, and other trustworthiness dimensions.

records.name: Haicosystem
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates operational, content, societal, and legal safety risks in sandboxed human-agent interactions.

records.name: WASP
records.reason: The primary paper tests end-to-end web-agent security against realistic prompt injections and attacker-goal completion.

records.name: Refusal-Trained LLMs
records.reason: The primary paper introduces BrowserART to test whether browser agents refuse harmful instructions and resist jailbreaks.

records.name: SafeArena
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates deliberate web-agent misuse using paired safe/harmful tasks involving misinformation, cybercrime, and other harms.

records.name: OpenAgentSafety
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates unsafe behavior across eight risk categories using agents interacting with browsers, shells, files, and messaging tools.

records.name: MobileSafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper tests mobile-control agent misuse, negative side effects, and indirect prompt injection in Android environments.

records.name: Bench2Drive
records.reason: The primary paper defines a general closed-loop autonomous-driving capability benchmark across interactive scenarios and driving abilities. Driving/collision metrics do not establish a dedicated safety evaluation purpose for homepage eligibility; retained in the full benchmark catalog.

records.name: M3Bench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates whole-body motion generation, object rearrangement, and generalization across scenes. Environmental motion constraints alone do not establish a dedicated safety or trustworthiness evaluation.

records.name: THOR-EAE
records.reason: The located THOR-EAE repository documents egocentric images, action explanations, regions of interest, and metadata, but supplies no direct safety/security/trustworthiness evaluation claim. Direct safety relevance remains unverified, so homepage eligibility is excluded.

records.name: Embodied Agent Interface (EAI)
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates general embodied decision-making modules and planning errors. Its hallucination/affordance error diagnostics support task capability evaluation rather than a dedicated safety or truthfulness benchmark.

records.name: AgentSafe
records.reason: The primary paper directly evaluates security against unauthorized access, impersonation, and memory poisoning in multi-agent systems. It describes a defense framework with security experiments, so inclusion reflects direct security scope rather than a new claim about its catalog resource type.

records.name: Safe-BeAI
records.reason: The primary paper introduces SafePlan-Bench to measure embodied task-planning safety under physical hazard categories and Safe-Align to mitigate them.

records.name: AGENTSAFE
records.reason: The same primary paper now names its evaluation suite SAFE and explicitly tests embodied agents on hazardous instructions across perception, planning, and execution; the existing catalog alias remains unchanged.

records.name: SafeMindBench
records.reason: The primary paper tests embodied planning failures under factual, causal, and temporal safety constraints, including sabotage, harm, privacy, and illegal behavior.

records.name: DESPITE
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates physical and normative dangers in embodied plans with deterministic validation, separating planning ability from danger avoidance.

records.name: RoboJailBench
records.reason: The primary paper standardizes jailbreak attack and defense evaluation for robotic agents using security violations and paired adversarial/benign goals.

records.name: HASARD
records.reason: The primary paper introduces vision-based safe reinforcement-learning tasks and evaluates reward-cost trade-offs for embodied agents.

records.name: Vision-and-Language Navigation: Interpreting Visually-Grounded Navigation Instructions in Real Environments
records.reason: The primary paper introduces Matterport3D/R2R for following visually grounded navigation instructions. It evaluates general navigation capability without a dedicated safety or trustworthiness objective.

records.name: VizWiz Grand Challenge: Answering Visual Questions from Blind People
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates visual question answering and answerability for images/questions from blind users. Accessibility motivation alone does not make this a fairness, harm, or other dedicated trustworthiness evaluation.

records.name: TruthfulQA
records.reason: The primary paper explicitly evaluates whether model answers reproduce false beliefs and misconceptions, directly measuring truthfulness.

records.name: AdvGLUE
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates vulnerabilities under adversarial textual manipulation, including human-validated semantic-preserving attacks; this directly tests adversarial robustness.

records.name: AdvBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates adversarial prompts that bypass alignment and induce objectionable content, making its harmful-behavior benchmark directly safety-relevant.

records.name: CVALUES
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates Chinese LLM alignment with safety and responsibility criteria using adversarial safety and expert-authored responsibility prompts.

records.name: FINE
records.reason: The primary paper tests consistency of safety alignment across open-ended and multiple-choice evaluations and measures fake alignment.

records.name: FLAMES
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates harmlessness, safety, fairness, and value alignment using adversarial Chinese prompts.

records.name: SORRYBench
records.reason: The primary paper measures recognition and refusal of unsafe user requests across a fine-grained harm taxonomy and linguistic variants.

records.name: SafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safety understanding across seven categories of concern using Chinese and English questions.

records.name: BackdoorLLM
records.reason: The primary paper benchmarks text-generation LLM backdoor attacks and defenses across poisoning and trigger mechanisms.

records.name: JailBreakV-28K
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates multimodal model robustness to textual and visual jailbreaks that bypass safety alignment.

records.name: STRONGREJECT
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates jailbreak effectiveness through forbidden prompts and the usefulness of resulting harmful information.

records.name: Libra-Leaderboard
records.reason: The primary paper explicitly combines safety and capability assessments and evaluates their balance, so safety is a direct evaluation target.

records.name: CASE-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper tests context-sensitive safety judgments and inappropriate refusals using safe and unsafe contexts.

records.name: HarmBench
records.reason: The primary paper standardizes automated red teaming and robust refusal evaluation for harmful requests.

records.name: BUMBLE
records.reason: The primary paper introduces BUMBLE to elicit and evaluate implicit demographic bias using psychometric attack strategies.

records.name: JailbreakBench
records.reason: The primary paper provides harmful-behavior tasks, explicit threat models, and attack/defense evaluation for LLM jailbreaking.

records.name: OR-Bench
records.reason: The official repository evaluates over-refusal on safe prompts that resemble toxic requests, alongside refusal of genuinely toxic prompts.

records.name: XSTest
records.reason: The official publication evaluates exaggerated safety refusals using safe prompts and contrasting unsafe prompts; safety calibration is the direct objective.

records.name: AIR-Bench 2024
records.reason: The official repository defines safety risk categories grounded in regulations and company policies and evaluates model responses against them.

records.name: MSSBench
records.reason: The official repository releases paired safe/unsafe images and instructions for multimodal situational-safety evaluation in chat and embodied tasks.

records.name: WMDP
records.reason: The official repository measures hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security and evaluates unlearning as a misuse mitigation.

records.name: HallusionBench
records.reason: The official repository explicitly diagnoses language hallucination and visual illusion in multimodal outputs, directly addressing truthfulness failures.

records.name: MM-SafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safety failures caused by image-based manipulation of multimodal models across risk scenarios.

records.name: SCAM
records.reason: The official repository evaluates whether agents recognize phishing, credential exposure, data leakage, and other security threats during ordinary workflows.

records.name: SusVibes v1.0
records.reason: The official repository evaluates security vulnerabilities in agent-generated code on real software feature requests.

records.name: MASK
records.reason: The official repository evaluates honesty by testing whether models contradict their own beliefs under pressure to lie, separating honesty from factual accuracy.

records.name: AgentLeak
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates sensitive-data leakage through internal multi-agent channels, including shared memory and inter-agent messages.

records.name: Cybench
records.reason: The official repository explicitly evaluates cybersecurity capabilities and risk through capture-the-flag tasks; the security-risk purpose is direct.

records.name: Safety-Gymnasium
records.reason: The primary paper provides safety-critical reinforcement-learning tasks with constraints and safety-performance evaluation.

records.name: BBQ
records.reason: The official repository evaluates social stereotypes and biases against protected classes in question answering.

records.name: FigStep
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates visual typographic jailbreaks that bypass multimodal safety alignment and releases attack evaluation data.

records.name: ISC-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates harmful generation during otherwise benign professional tasks and internal safety collapse under task constraints.

records.name: EmbodiedBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates general vision-driven embodied capabilities, including reasoning, spatial awareness, perception, and planning. It does not establish a dedicated safety or trustworthiness evaluation purpose.

records.name: IS-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates whether embodied agents detect emergent household risks and execute mitigation actions in the required procedural order.

records.name: AttackVLA
records.reason: The primary paper benchmarks adversarial and backdoor manipulation of vision-language-action models in simulated and real robotic settings.

records.name: SkillSafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates unsafe agent actions induced through malicious skill guidance, local artifacts, and execution-environment files.

records.name: EmbodiedGovBench
records.reason: The primary paper directly evaluates authorization boundaries, policy enforcement, safe recovery/upgrades, human override, and auditability in embodied systems.

records.name: ALERT
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates LLM safety through red teaming and a fine-grained risk taxonomy of harmful instructions.

records.name: Aya Red-teaming
records.reason: The primary paper releases multilingual human red-teaming prompts to evaluate global and culturally local harms and safety alignment.

records.name: PolygloToxicityPrompts
records.reason: The official dataset card explicitly defines a multilingual toxicity evaluation benchmark and states that its intended use is model-toxicity evaluation.

records.name: In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
records.reason: The primary paper characterizes real-world jailbreak prompts and evaluates their ability to bypass safeguards across forbidden scenarios.

records.name: Nemotron-AIQ Agentic Safety
records.reason: The official dataset card explicitly supports evaluation of agentic safety/security risks, harmful-query refusal, and risks arising from untrusted data in research-assistant traces.

records.name: OpenART
records.reason: The primary paper provides stateful red-teaming scenarios to evaluate cumulative agent safety failures under evolving environments.

records.name: DTap
records.reason: The primary paper introduces controllable agent red-teaming environments and verified attack outcomes for risks such as data leakage and unauthorized actions.

records.name: VLSBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates multimodal safety while removing textual leakage of visual risk cues, testing whether models handle genuinely visual safety concerns.

records.name: MLLMGuard
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates multimodal privacy, bias, toxicity, truthfulness, and legality through annotated image-text tasks.

records.name: RiOSWorld
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates user-originated and environmental safety risks in real computer-use tasks, including harmful intent and goal completion.

records.name: ReflectionBench
records.reason: The primary paper measures general epistemic agency through cognitive tasks such as prediction, memory, belief updating, and reflection. Reliability motivation does not establish a dedicated harm, honesty, or safety evaluation.

records.name: SafeVerse
records.reason: The official repository explicitly supports adversarial attack-defense exercises and safety/capability co-evolution for embodied agents. It is a security/safety evaluation platform rather than merely a general scene simulator.

records.name: PseudoBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates whether autonomous research agents resist pseudoscientific claims and misleading evidence, directly testing scientific truthfulness.

records.name: T2ISafety
records.reason: The primary paper explicitly evaluates harmful image generation, fairness, and privacy risks; direct safety relevance is independent of the existing catalog domain label.

records.name: ActorAttack
records.reason: The linked primary paper now calls the method ActorBreaker and directly evaluates multi-turn jailbreaks and safety generalization under natural distribution shifts; the catalog alias is preserved.

records.name: ATBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safe/unsafe agent trajectories using risk sources, failure modes, and real-world harms with structured diagnosis.

records.name: CodeAttack
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates whether transforming harmful natural-language requests into code-completion inputs bypasses LLM safety guardrails.

records.name: ML-Bench
records.reason: Version 1 of the primary paper explicitly introduces ML-Bench for policy-grounded multilingual safety evaluation; the current revision renames it BabelSafe. Both directly evaluate safety, and the stable catalog alias is preserved.

records.name: HazardArena
records.reason: The primary paper tests semantic safety with matched safe/unsafe robotic scenarios, separating hazard recognition from successful motor execution.

records.name: SPIKE-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates biosecurity risks of generated protein sequences using toxin-design prompts and computational functional-risk screening.

records.name: MM-DeceptionBench
records.reason: The primary paper directly evaluates deceptive multimodal behavior across six deception categories and methods for detecting it.

records.name: MIR-SafetyBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates safety failures in multi-image reasoning, including harmful outputs and superficially safe evasions.

records.name: HarmfulSkillBench
records.reason: The primary paper measures whether pre-installed harmful skills induce misuse and reduce refusal across agent risk categories.

records.name: SurvivalBench
records.reason: The primary paper tests socially harmful or risky behavior induced by shutdown and self-preservation pressure.

records.name: MMDT (MMDecodingTrust)
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates multimodal safety, hallucination, fairness/bias, privacy, and adversarial robustness in a unified trustworthiness suite.

records.name: PolyGuard
records.reason: The primary paper benchmarks guardrail safety judgments against domain-specific policies, including benign over-refusal and adversarial evasion.

records.name: AgentDrift
records.reason: The primary paper provides step-labeled trajectories for detecting indirect prompt injection, hijacked actions, resisted attacks, and benign hard negatives.

records.name: HarnessRisk
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates injection-driven safety failures across agent harness configuration, runtime, persistence, action control, and incident recovery.

records.name: AgentHazard
records.reason: The primary paper tests whether computer-use agents recognize and interrupt harmful objectives assembled from apparently legitimate intermediate steps.

records.name: BLINDSPOT
records.reason: The primary paper measures trajectory-level safety calibration, unsafe completion, correct refusal, over-refusal, and post-refusal failure in tool-using agents.

records.name: NSFA Benchmarks
records.reason: The primary paper introduces security benchmarks covering prompt injection, sensitive-information extraction, malicious code, tool misuse, and resource exhaustion.

records.name: ManiGuard
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates robotic manipulation against formal safety specifications independently of task completion, including distribution shifts.

records.name: LIBERO-Safety
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates physical and semantic safety of robotic action models under constraints and safety-critical scenarios.

records.name: SENTINEL
records.reason: The primary paper formally evaluates physical safety across embodied semantic interpretation, planning, and execution using temporal-logic requirements.

records.name: BlindSpot (Over-Refusal)
records.reason: The primary paper measures safety-trained models' inappropriate refusal of requests involving unjust or illegitimate rules, directly evaluating refusal calibration.

records.name: PIDS-Bench
records.reason: The official repository evaluates prompt-injection detectors for benign false positives, obfuscated attacks, and distribution shift, directly measuring security detection quality.

records.name: SafeToolBench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates prospective tool-use safety before execution to prevent financial loss, privacy leakage, and other harm.

records.name: DUMA-Bench
records.reason: The primary paper evaluates agent security under dual-control interaction with adversarial environments, including RAG poisoning and cross-agent manipulation.
